To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bed permeability significantly affects the distribution of normal form- induced stress, and that the transport of turbulent kinetic toward the subsurface flow is driven mainly by the fluctuations of pressure.

the flow resistance of a porous bed is significantly affected by bed permeability, and that this is mainly due to the different distributions of normal form-induced stresses between the permeable surface and impermeable surface cases.

bed permeability significantly affects flow resistance in the hydraulics rough regime and that the transport of turbulent kinetic-energy from the surface toward the subsurface flow is mainly due to pressure fluctuations, whereas the transport due to velocity fluctuations is limited.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of turbulence structure in open-channel flows over porous and impermeable surfaces.
the interaction between surface and subsurface flows in open channel flows, and the influence of this interaction on the structure of the turbulent boundary layer.
the study of the structure of turbulent flow in open channels with rough beds and the effect that permeability has on the flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the permeable bed is characterized by a more energetic surface flow than the impermeable one, whereas the subsurface flow is less energetic and dissipative.

the surface flow and the subsurface flows are not completely independent from each other, but rather that the surface flow is the dominant one, as it drives the subsurface flow, and that it is also the subsurface flow which is responsible for the dissipation of the turbulence generated at the surface.
permeability of the bed affects the flow structure in the entire depth of the flow, and not only at the bed surface, where the permeable bed acts as a roughness element.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface flow over a permeable bed is not only affected by the bed permeability but also by the subsurface flow which, in turn, is affected by the surface flow.
the surface flow over the permeable bed induces a strong turbulence in the subsurface flow, and this turbulence is mainly driven by pressure fluctuations.
permeable beds are characterized by a more intense surface flow, and by a more intense subsurface flow than impermeable beds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the permeable bed can be viewed as a system where the surface and subsurface flow interact with each other and influence each other in a way that is not possible for the impermeable bed.
the surface and subsurface flows in open channel flows are strongly coupled.
permeability affects both the surface flow and subsurface flow, which in turn influence each other through the exchange of turbulent kinetic energy.
